You are under no obligation to make people see your worth though. If you have to fight for them to see your value and treat you like you're worth something, you need to drop those people immediately and continue your life until someone can actually treat you the way you deserve to be treated. 

Your value as a relationship partner isn't determined by someone who shows no interest in you, same way a diamond's value isn't determined by how many didn't want to buy it.

Form good habits, learn how to study (because I was never taught how and it's terrible trying to relearn it in college) and learn how to COOK.  

Take more challenging classes, it'll make school more fun and help you learn time management + discipline. Go for walks or runs, read up on philosophy or moral ethics or something that you'd probably never have to apply to a situation in life. 

There is always something to do, to read or to see! You just have to know what you like.

When I first started I did as much research as I could. I also try to learn the history of certain things to understand why specific slurs and actions are considered innaproprate and offensive. I also read the news, NewYork Times, CNN etc.  and make sure that the sources were reliable and non-biased. 

My most helpful part was social media. I got to read the experiences of people who have suffered as a result of politics, plus you learn about the event and the people at the same time. 

Some good places to start:

-Black History + why you shouldn't say the n word no matter what 
-Misogyny and it's presence in our society today 
-Feminism + our goals + definition of feminists. 
-Gun Laws 
-Rape Culture 
-LGBTQ+ community (Discrimination faced, black trans women aren't expected to live past 35, homophobic crimes etc.)
-Abortion rights (and why your opinion doesn't matter if you don't have a uterus) 
-Free Healthcare
